title: Chemical Services Intake
intro: Five questions. MBS FUEL's Department of Chemical Services will work out how much of your eating has already been replaced, and offer to replace the rest.
privacy: Your answers stay on this device. Nothing here is sent anywhere, no account is made, and no email or phone number is asked for or required to see your result.
missingLabel: Chemical Services requires an answer here:

questions.label: In a normal week, how many meals do you eat standing up, walking, or at a desk?

options.label: None, I sit down to eat

questions.label: How often does a drink stand in for a meal?
Roughly what share of your food spending goes on powders, bars and replacement drinks?
questions.help: A range only. No exact figure is asked for.

questions.label: Which flavour should the lab mix live on Wednesday's show?
questions.help: This one is a vote. It is the only answer here that changes what gets broadcast.

bands.text: Unconverted. You are still eating food, in a room, with a chair. Chemical Services regards this as a market opportunity.
Partially converted. Meals are already becoming errands. The department is encouraged.
Substantially converted. Eating has been folded into the working day, which is exactly where the department likes it.
Fully converted. There is nothing left for MBS FUEL to replace, and the department would like to congratulate you on this in an advertisement.
No formula issued. Keep the chair. (MBS FUEL is a fiction. Nothing here is nutritional advice, and no product exists.)
One serving daily, taken in place of whichever meal is least defended. (MBS FUEL is a fiction. Nothing here is nutritional advice, and no product exists.)
Two servings daily, with the third meal retained for morale. (MBS FUEL is a fiction. Nothing here is nutritional advice, and no product exists.)
The full stack: every meal, every day, forever, at a price that rises annually. (MBS FUEL is a fiction. Nothing here is nutritional advice, and no product exists.)

outcomes.label: What that actually adds up to

map.never: No arithmetic to do. A meal is still a meal here, which is rarer than the advertising suggests.
map.weekly: Call it one or two a week: somewhere around six or eight meals a month that are a purchase rather than a meal. Small, and worth knowing the size of.
map.most_days: Most days is roughly twenty meals a month you are not choosing so much as buying. That is the number the category is built on.
map.most_meals: Most meals is most of the roughly ninety eating occasions in a month, handed over to whoever mixes the powder. Worth knowing the size of, whatever you decide about it.

outcomes.label: What you changed about Wednesday

map.original: Your vote goes to Original. If it wins, Wednesday's mix is the one the ads use.
map.citrus: Your vote goes to Citrus Compliance. If it wins, Wednesday's mix is the orange one.
map.chalk: Your vote goes to Vanilla Chalk. If it wins, the lab has to drink it on camera.
map.unflavoured: Your vote goes to Unflavoured. If it wins, Wednesday's show is going to be quiet.

outcomes.fallback: You did not vote, so Wednesday's flavour is somebody else's decision.
